title: On Practice Period
speaker: Nomon Tim Burnett
summary: Nomon Tim Burnett takes up Eihei Dogen's writing on the ninety-day practice period as the winter practice period begins next week. Nomon reads Dogen's lines on the lineage of practice periods running from the Buddha through Bodhidharma to America, and on how joining one means seeing and practicing Buddha. Nomon suggests showing up as Buddha from the first clack of the clackers, not to get something, and offers the hub and rim of a wheel for Talus as shuso. Nomon then lays out the schedule, the seven factors of awakening, a memorial for the musician Majnuun, and a request to practice the room from the inside of the body.
